identity.description: Klaviyo: marketing automation / email & SMS platform. developers.klaviyo.com is its official developer portal, and the docs describe the Klaviyo product (profiles, lists, campaigns, flows, Klaviyo App Marketplace).
identity.identity_notes: Official developer portal and product pages match the named app. Only the portal and Klaviyo-hosted MCP/SDK pages were checked directly; the product description is from the docs and search results, not a full fetch of the marketing site.

auth.oauth_flows: Authorization code flow with PKCE (per the OAuth setup page). Authorization endpoint https://www.klaviyo.com/oauth/authorize; token endpoint https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token.
auth.token_refresh: Access tokens are valid for 1 hour (subject to change; use expires_in from /token). Refresh tokens remain valid until the app is uninstalled. Refresh calls are limited to 10 per minute.
auth.scopes_notes: Scopes are per resource, for example lists:read and lists:write. Webhooks need webhooks:read/webhooks:write; event subscriptions need events:read (from search snippet, not fetched). Private keys are created with Custom, Read-Only, or Full Access scopes. Public keys (6-character company ID) are for client-side /client endpoints only and cannot access protected data.

access.production_restrictions: Marketplace listing requires OAuth (per OAuth docs). Webhook API access is reportedly limited to Advanced KDP customers and Klaviyo app partners (search snippet of v2026-07-15 docs, not fetched). Creating/managing private keys and OAuth apps requires an Owner, Admin, or Manager role, so a developer needs one of those roles on the account they test against.

api.rate_limits: Two windows: burst (short) and steady (long). Numeric limits not established.
api.limitations: Resource list and read/write coverage were not verified from a fetched page, so breadth stays Unknown. Webhook API access appears restricted (see access). Webhook limit of 10 per account comes from a 2024 page and may be outdated. JSON:API format used. /api endpoints need a private API key; /client endpoints use public keys. Webhooks support is confirmed by the docs overview but details come from search snippets.
